findings: The current annual catalogue verifies 60 EC in year one and identifies 55 distinct EC for year two. The year-two list repeats the first-year 5 EC Humanities in a Digital World course. The previous annual guide and the transitional table do not confirm a distinct replacement for September 2026 entrants. Current year-three course records identify 10 EC Academic Reading and Writing in semester one, the 10 EC thesis and zero-credit seminar in semester two, and split 15 EC elective placeholders. The concentration parent gives 15 EC while its two branches each specify 10 EC and programme prose describes two advanced courses. Thesis and seminar normally follow the first two years and advanced academic writing. Earlier programme wording about an open first semester does not establish the current entrant timetable.

interests.text: learning Dutch to a high academic level
interests.assessment: Academic Dutch is a direct goal, with progression beyond beginner instruction.
Dutch historical and cultural study is an independent goal.
Society and identity recur in debate and film.

interests.text: the Dutch language in an international context
interests.assessment: Acquisition, history and multilingual use are stable linguistic interests.

interests.text: how Dutch culture relates to other countries and cultures
interests.assessment: The programme encourages cultural comparison in Dutch contexts.

interests.text: understanding the Netherlands as a non-native speaker
interests.assessment: Study explicitly targets non-native speakers.
Speech and listening progress into academic presentation.
Written Dutch progresses into disciplinary reading and writing.
Practical language training and the study of second-language acquisition are distinct.
Introductory linguistics and Dutch structures are taught.
Dutch literature has two distinct historical units.
Historical study spans earlier and modern Netherlands.
The course examines Dutch art history.
Dutch painting is a dedicated component.
Film is used to study the Netherlands.
Newspapers and public debate support study of society.
The history of Dutch is directly taught.
The project is normally written in Dutch on a programme topic.

interests.text: whether Dutch is harder to learn for speakers of different languages
interests.assessment: Cross-language differences illustrate acquisition questions.

interests.text: Dutch debates about identity and society
interests.assessment: Specific debates illustrate the recurring Dutch society interest.
Immersion illustrates language learning, with no separate course or outcome inferred.
Named artists illustrate the national painting sequence.
Translation is a trajectory, without an inferred qualification.

interests.text: teaching Dutch as a second language
interests.assessment: Teaching is an outcome context. The acquisition course is independently verified.
Consulting and communication are transferable outcome contexts.

interests.text: further study in Dutch language or culture
interests.assessment: Later study remains an individual trajectory.
